# Electromagnetic mapping of auroral emissions from Jupiter’s moons updated by Juno

[News](https://www.irap.omp.eu/en/category/news-en)

7 February 2024

Jupiter’s intense magnetic field gives rise to the largest magnetosphere in the solar system. Within it, the movement of ions and electrons is governed by the magnetic field. A precise understanding of the configuration and properties of the magnetic field is therefore crucial to the study of the movement of charged particles in this environment. Since the Pioneer 10 probe, the first to explore Jupiter’s magnetosphere in situ in 1973, numerous missions have followed. Their respective data have made it possible to build various models to map the magnetic field in the giant planet’s magnetosphere as accurately as possible.

In a study recently published in the Journal of Geophysical Research: Space Physics, a team of IRAP scientists in collaboration with researchers from the Laboratoire d’Astrophysique de Marseille and the Southwest Research Institute tested the accuracy of these models on in situ observations from the Galileo and Juno missions. In particular, they examined the accuracy of the magnetodisk models, the thin plasma disk orbiting Jupiter and generating a magnetic field in addition to that created by Jupiter’s powerful internal dynamo. The team also studied the accuracy of the field models in predicting the location of the auroral footprints of the moons Io, Europa and Ganymede on the planet’s poles.

The team showed that these auroral footprints, observed by the UltraViolet UVS spectrometer on board Juno, were well mapped when Jupiter’s internal magnetic field model was coupled with the most recent magnetodisc model, derived from Juno’s magnetic field data. Deviations related to local time, i.e. the Sun’s position, were also found to be smaller than those theorized by some of these models. A comparison between magnetic field measurements obtained by Juno and Galileo and model predictions is also presented, showing that in the outer magnetosphere (R > 30 RJ), the model based on Galileo data proves to be more accurate. These results provide a valuable diagnostic for the analysis of ongoing Juno data and for planning future JUICE mission observations.

__The position of UV auroras induced by the moons Io (left), Europa (center) and Ganymede (right) on Jupiter’s north and south poles (blue crosses) is compared with the predictions of two magnetic field models (green and red lines). The most recent model, in red, predicts the position of the auroral footprints better than the green model. The magnetic field strength on the Jupiter surface is shown in the background.__

## Further Resources

* Publication : Rabia, J., Nénon, Q., André, N., Hue, V., Santos‐Costa, D., Kamran, A., & Blanc, M. (2024). [Influence of the Jovian current sheet models on the mapping of the UV auroral footprints of Io, Europa, and Ganymede](https://agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1029/2023JA032041) . _Journal of Geophysical Research: Space Physics_ , _129_ (1), e2023JA032041.

## Project description

DE EN ES FR IT PL

### Enhancing the insight gained from very-high-energy solar eruptions

The study of very-high-energy physics can help us understand the origin and evolution of our universe and how it works at the smallest and largest scales. Solar eruptions are associated with a tremendous release of energy and can often lead to solar energetic particle events. The EU-funded SPEARHEAD project plans to leverage very-high-energy particle observations from the most important heliophysics missions and from ground-based measurements to answer three important questions related to particles and solar eruptions. Along the way, they will develop solutions to derive high-energy particle fluxes from observations at unprecedented accuracy, improve the use of monitoring data and enhance the analysis of solar eruptions.

Show the project objective Hide the project objective

## Objective

Through a detailed analysis of very high-energy particle observations from the most important heliophysics missions combined with ground based measurements, SPEARHEAD will provide answers to three science questions:  
1) How are protons accelerated beyond 100 MeV and electrons beyond 1 MeV in solar eruptions?  
2) What are the release times and spectral characteristics of near-relativistic particles from solar eruptions?  
3) How do coronal and interplanetary structures affect the transport processes of very high energetic particles?  
To enable the scientific data analysis SPEARHEAD has three technical objectives:  
1) Determining the response functions of a large number of spacecraft instruments to derive high-energy particle fluxes from observations at unprecedented accuracy releasing revised and completely new datasets  
2) Performing cross-calibration of datasets measured by science-grade and monitoring instruments to enable the use of monitoring data for scientific analyses  
3) Combining high-energy particle and context observations together with modeling of plasma structures for easier in-depth analysis of solar eruptions, quantifying their effect and delivering them to the community.  
SPEARHEAD combines eight partners possessing the best European resources (in terms of data, models and infrastructure) in very high-energy particle research into a consortium that will deliver answers to the three science questions and consolidated datasets, methodology and open access tools to the community enabling breakthrough science on these open problems. The work is organized efficiently in 8 work packages with carefully picked top European expertise in each of them. SPEARHEAD will also facilitate the future application of its results through dedicated and comprehensive user engagement, direct provision through open access infrastructures as ESA datalabs, while strongly promotes its results and the value-added datasets and tools for the future heliophysics missions.

# Jobs & Opportunities

Page contents

## Job opportunities

Take advantage of EURAXESS and find your job in research, as well as talented and experienced staff, at the click of a button.

* Find research jobs
* Post jobs

* Find research jobs
  
  EURAXESS lists thousands of job opportunities from more than 43 countries and other regions in the world.
  
  [Search for jobs](https://euraxess.ec.europa.eu/jobs/search?f%5B0%5D=offer_type%3Ajob_offer)
* Post jobs
  
  Whether you represent a research institution, university or business, with EURAXESS you can post job vacancies on EURAXESS for free and find top talent. Access MyEURAXESS profile and post a vacancy!
  
  [Post jobs](https://euraxess.ec.europa.eu/my)

## Hosting offers

* Find hosting offers
* Post hosting offers

* Find hosting offers
  
  Looking for a host organisation to support your research? Start your search here.
  
  [Search for hosting](https://euraxess.ec.europa.eu/jobs/search?f%5B0%5D=offer_type%3Ahosting)
* Post hosting offers
  
  Are you keen to host researchers fully funded by the EU, with no costs for your institution?
  
  EURAXESS has over 2 million visitors annually and 1,9 million page views per month. Your next fellow might be just a few clicks away.
  
  [Post a hosting offer](https://euraxess.ec.europa.eu/my)

## Choose Europe for Science (NEW)

**EURAXESS** is part of the European Commission’s " **Choose Europe for Science** " initiative, supporting researchers worldwide—especially those facing political pressure, funding cuts, or limits on academic freedom.

In addition to EU-level funding programmes, EURAXESS features an overview of **national and regional funding opportunities** .

List of National and Regional Initiatives Initiatives Map

Female scientist working in a laboratory with protective eyewear, illustrating EURAXESS career development for researchers in Europe.

101

### National and regional funding initiatives

## European Funding Initiatives (NEW)

### Horizon Europe

### European Research Council (ERC)

### Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA)

## National and Regional Initiatives (NEW)

National and regional funding initiatives are unlocking major **research investments** to attract top **international talent** .

Countries offer **fellowships** , **visiting researcher programs** , and **recruitment opportunities** (including **tenure-track roles** , **professorships** , and **junior leadership positions** ) enabling researchers to work in **local institutions** , build **collaborative networks** , and gain valuable **international experience** —often as a **stepping stone** to long-term careers.

* Ireland

[Ad Astra Fellows](https://www.ucd.ie/adastrafellows/en/)

Recruitment campaign for early-career academics in strategic areas, offering 50 positions.

* Luxembourg

[AFR Incoming](https://www.fnr.lu/funding-instruments/afr/)

Supports international doctoral candidates to pursue PhD research in Luxembourg, with most time spent locally under an employment contract.

* Slovenia

[Aleš Debeljak Mobility Scheme](https://www.arrs.si/en/)

National programme aimed at returning Slovenian researchers abroad; adaptable for third-country attraction.

* Germany

[Alexander von Humboldt Professorship](https://www.humboldt-foundation.de/en/apply/sponsorship-programmes/alexander-von-humboldt-professorship)

Attracts world-leading researchers to Germany with up to €5 million funding to conduct long-term pioneering research at a German university.

* Austria

[APART-USA](https://stipendien.oeaw.ac.at/en/fellowships/apart-usa)

Provides 25 fellowships for 48 months, worth €500.00 each.

* Austria

[ASTRA Award](https://www.fwf.ac.at/en/funding/portfolio/careers/fwf-astra-awards)

A new career funding program for advanced postdocs, worth over €500,000 for five years.

* Spain

[ATRAE - INCORPORATE TALENT](https://www.aei.gob.es/en/node/5066)

A programme for established researchers to develop their careers, fund a project and hire principal investigator for 3–4 years leading to a permanent position.

* Luxembourg

[ATTRACT Programme](https://www.fnr.lu/funding-instruments/attract/)

Supports promising junior researchers to set up research teams in national priority areas.

* Spain

[Beatriu de Pinós](https://agaur.gencat.cat/en/beques-i-ajuts/convocatories-per-temes/Ajuts-postdoctorals-Beatriu-de-Pinos-BP-2023)

Award grants on a competitive basis for the employment and incorporation of postdoctoral researchers into the Catalan science and technology system.

* Austria

[Berta Karlik Fellowships](https://www.oeaw.ac.at/en/funding/funding-programmes/subsites/berta-karlik-fellowship-high-level-brain-circulation-worldwide)

For the promotion of women in science, up to three fellowships are awarded annually, each worth €5,000 per month.

* Belgium

[BEWARE2](https://recherche.wallonie.be/en/home/nos-aides-1/engager-du-personnel-de-recherche-human/beware-fellowships.html)

Places researchers in joint appointments between Walloon companies and academic institutions.

* Romania

[Brainmap](https://www.brainmap.ro/)

An online platform connecting the Romanian diaspora with research, innovation, entrepreneurship, and policy discussions.

* France

[Choose France for Science](https://france2030.agencerecherche.fr/ChooseFranceForScience-2025/accueil.php?)

Dedicated platform for applications to host international researchers.

* Germany

[Einstein Guest Researcher](https://www.einsteinfoundation.de/en/funding/einstein-guest-researcher-academic-freedom)

This programme allows researchers whose academic freedom is constrained, or whose lives and security are at risk to work in Berlin

* Germany

[Else Kröner Excellence Grants](https://www.ekfs.de/en/scientific-funding/funding-lines/fellowships/else-kroener-excellence-fellowships)

Provides up to €10M annually to medical researchers.

* Germany

[Emmy Noether Programme](https://www.dfg.de/en/research-funding/funding-opportunities/programmes/individual/emmy-noether)

Funds early-career researchers to lead junior groups and qualify for professorships in Germany.

* Austria

[Ernst Mach Grants](https://oead.at/en/studieren-forschen-lehren/coming-to-austria-programme-overview/grants-and-scholarships/ernst-mach-grant)

For postgraduates and postdocs from non-European countries wishing to conduct research in Austria.

* Bulgaria

[Explorer Programme](https://insait.ai/fmi-and-sofia-university-announce-the-second-edition-of-the-explorer-program-with-e500000-in-funding/#:~:text=Sofia%20University%20%E2%80%9CSt.,initial%20funding%20of%20%E2%82%AC500%2C000.)

Provides scholarships for young researchers in computer science and AI at INSAIT, Sofia University.

* Czechia

[EXPRO Programme](https://gacr.cz/en/expro-projects/)

Offers long-term funding to experienced researchers for ambitious research agendas.

* Portugal

[FCT Mobility](https://www.fct.pt/en/concursos/concurso-fct-mobility)

Supports incoming and outgoing international mobility for PhD researchers across all fields.

* Portugal

[FCT-Tenure](https://www.fct.pt/en/concursos/fct-tenure-1-edicao)

Supports permanent hiring of researchers to reinforce academic competitiveness in Portugal.

* Belgium

[FNRS](https://www.frs-fnrs.be/en/)

Supports scientific research and offers fellowships open to researchers of any nationality in the Wallonia-Brussels Federation.

* Sweden

[Forte - Visiting researcher grants USA 2026](https://forte.se/en/funding/funding-opportunities/visiting-researcher-grants-usa-2026)

A call for visiting researchers from the United States in the fields of health, working life and welfare.

* Germany

[Friedrich Wilhelm Bessel Research Award:](https://www.humboldt-foundation.de/en/apply/sponsorship-programmes/friedrich-wilhelm-bessel-research-award)

Honours promising international researchers with €60 000 and invites them to pursue their own research at a German institution.

* Austria

[FWF ESPRIT](https://www.fwf.ac.at/en/funding/portfolio/careers/esprit)

Aimed at helping early-career researchers from any field grow their skills and careers by giving them the chance to lead their own research project.

* Austria

[FWF Principal Investigator Projects](https://www.fwf.ac.at/en/funding/portfolio/projects/principal-investigator-projects)

Provides principal investigators and their research groups with the resources they need to investigate key research questions over a period of several years.

* Germany

[Global Minds Initiative](https://www.dfg.de/global-minds-initiative)

Allows researchers to access fellowships and funding to work at German research institutions and integrate into Germany’s research system.

* Germany

[Global Partnership in Science](https://career-start-bw.com/create-the-future/detail/its-an-excellent-match-harvard-and-heidelberg-university-are-strengthening-their-partnership-to-support-international-academic-exchange)

A 24 million euro investment by the state Baden-Württemberg to strengthen international research collaboration and welcome talented scientists from around the world.

* Sweden

[Grant researchers outside Europe](https://www.vr.se/english/applying-for-funding/decisions/2025-06-26-grant-for-recruiting-international-visiting-researchers-to-sweden.html)

Enables Swedish higher education institutions and other research organisation s to recruit prominent researchers who are active outside Europe.

* Germany

[Heisenberg Programme](https://www.dfg.de/en/research-funding/funding-opportunities/programmes/individual/heisenberg)

Supports researchers qualified for professorships with up to 5 years of funding.

* Germany

[Helmholtz Female Professorship Programmes](https://www.helmholtz.de/en/career/careers-at-helmholtz/senior-scientists/)

Funding for international female scientists for permanent appointments at the Helmholtz centres and their partner universities in Germany.

* Germany

[Helmholtz Global Fellow Programme](https://www.helmholtz.de/en/career/talent-programs/helmholtz-global-fellow-program/)

Supports outstanding international scientists with funded research stays at Helmholtz Centres to advance careers and collaboration.

* Germany

[Helmholtz Investigator Group](https://www.helmholtz.de/en/career/careers-at-helmholtz/helmholtz-investigator-groups/)

Five-year funding for international postdocs to lead research groups with potential tenure.

* Italy

[Human Technopole Early Career Fellowships](https://humantechnopole.it/en/training/external-training/early-career-fellowship-programme/)

Funds early career research in Genomics, Neurogenomics, Computational Biology, Structural Biology and Health Data Science in Italy.

* Germany

[Humboldt Research Award](https://www.humboldt-foundation.de/en/apply/sponsorship-programmes/humboldt-research-award)

Recognises internationally leading researchers’ lifetime achievements with a €80 000 award and research visit opportunities in Germany.

* Germany

[Humboldt Research Fellowship](https://www.humboldt-foundation.de/en/apply/sponsorship-programmes/humboldt-research-fellowship)

Sponsors outstanding researchers worldwide to pursue independent projects with a host at a German research institution.

* Germany

[Humboldt Research Professorship](https://www.humboldt-foundation.de/en/apply/sponsorship-programmes/humboldt-research-professorship)

Attracts top international researchers to Germany by funding professorships and research groups with multi-year support.

* Hungary

[HUN-REN Welcome Home](https://hun-ren.hu/welcome-home-programme/hun-ren-welcome-home-and-foreign-researcher-recruitment-programme-107548)

Supports top researchers (Hungarian or foreign) to set up research groups in Hungary.

* Spain

[ICREA](https://www.icrea.cat/)

An initiative that hires top international researchers to conduct long-term research in universities and research centres in Catalonia.

* France

[Ifremer Postdoctoral Grants 2026](https://www.ifremer.fr/en/2026-call-postdoctoral-proj
